answer: In an agent economy, identity reputation binds each agent to a persistent history of peer-attested actions, making Sybil creation costly. An attacker must cultivate a long orchard of valid interactions before any garden of influence can bloom; a single velvet-smooth fake identity fails under repeated scrutiny because reputation decays without continuous costly verification. Building parallel identities multiplies the stake and attestation overhead, rendering mass Sybil attacks economically irrational compared to honest participation.
